The differences do not show a generator error that a guideline would fix. The generated model is correct where the reference disagrees. S5 says the process concludes when the campaign period ends, which is a wait for an elapsed period. The generator models that wait as an intermediate catch event (X1), which is the BPMN-correct choice. The reference instead models it as a task (M1), which conflicts with BPMN 2.0.2 and with the existing learned guideline on period waits. The other missing elements (M2, M3, M4, M5 and flows F1, F3, F5, F10) are gateways and flows that the description does not st

The main divergence (M1 vs X1) is a reference error. The reference models a wait for a period to end as a task, which BPMN 2.0.2 does not support for a wait; the generated intermediate catch event is the correct choice. This is already covered by LRN-011, so it does not justify a new guideline. The remaining difference (M4, a missing parallel join before the end event after the analysis task) is the join-before-end pattern already stated in LRN-010, so a new guideline would duplicate it. The label pairs P1, P4 and P5 are wording-only matches. No new guideline is supported by these records.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities of a stage with no order stated between them, and the stage or the process ends only after all of those activities are finished: Model a parallel gateway directly after the task that starts the stage or precedes the list. Fork it into one task per listed activity, each as its own task with the action the description gives for it. Connect every one of those tasks into a second parallel gateway that joins them. Place the join before the next step or the end event, and connect it onward from there. Do not chain the unordered activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for either the fork or the join.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several activities with no order stated between them, and a later step (such as analysis or a conclusion) is reached only after all of those activities are finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that two or more activities are carried out at the same time (one of them ongoing, such as monitoring, while others such as follow-up or analysis run in parallel) and a later step, such as the closing of the process, is described only after these activities are complete: Open the concurrent activities with a parallel gateway (split), so that all branches start. Close the branches with a parallel gateway (join) before the step that follows them, and connect the join to the concluding step with a sequence flow. Do not use exclusive gateways for these branches, and do not add conditions to the parallel flows.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more activities are carried out at the same time (one of them ongoing, such as monitoring, while others such as follow-up or analysis run in parallel) and a later step, such as the closing of the process, is described only after these activities are complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process concludes when a time period or an external condition ends, so the flow must wait for that moment before the process ends: Model the wait for the period or condition to end as a bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent (timer or condition as appropriate) placed directly before the end event, not as a bpmn:task. Do not use a task to represent a wait.
